key_insight: PrivateBoost shows federated gradient boosting can learn effectively from just one medical record per participant while keeping raw patient data on-device.
clinical_relevance: This could help healthcare teams build privacy-preserving AI models from distributed patient devices without centralizing sensitive records.
method: Each device splits its local contribution into cryptographic secret shares.
Independent institutions hold the shares and only population-level sums are reconstructed.
Gradient boosting is trained in a federated setting without exposing individual records.
evidence_signal: Across four datasets with up to 70,692 participants, the approach matched centralized training, remained robust when up to 80% of participants were absent in a round, and used only a few megabytes of communication per patient.
watch_item: Real-world deployment depends on reliable coordination among institutions and devices, which may be challenging in settings with limited connectivity or operational complexity.
paper_title: Privacy Preserving Federated Gradient Boosting for Single Record Patient Devices
